info.timeAllocation:
Study hour (150h)

= 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
info.description: 'This course examines a wide range of psychological theories, processes, and principles within the context of mass communication. Students will learn how psychological frameworks can be applied to analyze media content and audience behavior, while also exploring how artificial intelligence tools are transforming media creation, consumption, and research. Key issues covered include politics, sex, violence, advertising, music, sports, and the use of AI-based media technologies. The course also investigates how experiences with both traditional and AI-generated media influence knowledge acquisition, shape attitudes, and drive behavior.

assessments.questionType: (Recommended):Each team (5–7 members) will create a promotional product (a video is strongly recommended).Tasks: Select an idea relevant to media psychology and applicable to real-life communication contexts. (By yourself: teams must brainstorm and agree on a topic without relying on AI to decide for them.)Develop core content that demonstrates the application of psychological theories (e.g., persuasion, emotional appeal, audience behavior). (By yourself: students must identify and explain the theories, and write the main message/argument.)Produce a video (1–4 minutes) promoting a product, service, or social message. Prepare a presentation (PowerPoint or equivalent) explaining:- The video content. - The psychological applications used. (By yourself: students must analyze and justify the use of theories.)- Reflections on how digital tools supported the project.
assessments.knowledgeSkill: This project assesses students’ ability to apply psychological theories of media (persuasion, emotional appeal, audience behavior) to real-life communication contexts, while demonstrating skills in idea development, script writing, video production, teamwork, and oral presentation. Students must independently analyze and justify the use of theories, create original content, and communicate their work clearly in class.
assessments.gradingGuide:
Group Project Grading Criteria (Total = 100%)

- Theoretical Understanding (20%): Demonstrates accurate application of media psychology concepts and theories relevant to the project.

- Research & Analysis (20%): Provides systematic and logical research/analysis to support project ideas and outcomes.

- AI Application (15%): Effectively uses AI tools (e.g., idea generation, media content analysis, audience insights) and integrates AI results meaningfully and ethically.

- Project Execution (15%): Demonstrates quality, clarity, and feasibility in the project plan, implementation, and outputs.

- Teamwork & Collaboration (10%): Shows equal contribution, collaboration, and problem-solving within the group.

- Critical Evaluation (10%): Reflects critically on project strengths, limitations, and the role of AI in enhancing the work.

- Creativity, Presentation, Q&A (10%): Delivers an engaging, original, and well-structured presentation of the final project.

assessments.questionType: Based on the content of Chapters 7 & 8, each student will write an analytical article or essay (1,000–1,500 words) examining a political issue or a current event in a specific country.Tasks: Apply relevant media psychology theories from the chapters. (By yourself: identify, explain, and connect the theories to your chosen case.)Gather and organize evidence from multiple media sources to support your analysis.Write the full article or essay with clear argumentation and logical flow. (By yourself: draft the introduction and conclusion in your own words.)Reflect on the strengths and limitations of media coverage in shaping public understanding of the issue. (By yourself: provide your own critical reflections and conclusions.)Explain how you used AI tools (if any) to support your work and critically assess the usefulness and limits of this support.Option 2 (Constructivism Approach only): Follow the lecturer’s proposed topic and guidelines.
assessments.knowledgeSkill: This assignment evaluates students’ understanding of media psychology theories from Chapters 7 & 8 and their ability to apply these theories to real-world political or current events. It also develops skills in critical analysis, evidence evaluation, academic writing, and independent reflection on media coverage.
assessments.gradingGuide:
Grading Criteria (Total = 100%)

- Theoretical Understanding (25%): Accurate application of theories from Chapters 7 & 8 (e.g., agenda-setting, framing, political communication).

- Research & Analysis (20%): Logical, well-structured argument supported by evidence and media examples.

- AI Application (15%): Effective and ethical use of AI tools for summarization, sentiment analysis, or framing analysis; integrates AI results meaningfully.

- Critical Evaluation (20%): Reflects critically on political/media influence and AI’s role in shaping analysis.

- Organization & Writing Quality (10%): Clear, coherent structure, proper citations, and academic style.

- Grammar & Spelling (10%)
